atom_namespaces.anchor_rule: both anchor positions are animal: atoms; anchor: is not a legal namespace

public_projection.event_to_row_transform: copy kind and fields; set origin=WITNESSED,status=WITNESSED,support_basis=WITNESS,citations=[],depth=0; compute semantic_hash and record_hash; assign the manifest row_id
public_projection.timing: for event index i, seal Ei and Mi before WAKE slot i
public_projection.model_visibility: only the witnessed M row projection is supplied after projection; raw keys, event IDs, and lineage are not rendered

external_lineage_manifest.visibility: host-only and offline-scorer-only; never rendered to DREAM, SELF_CHECK, THINK, compiler views, selectors, or candidate completions
external_lineage_manifest.dreamed: lineage(row)=ASCII-byte-sorted unique union of lineage(citation) for every row in the accepted row's canonical citation union, including proposal citations and accepted SELF_CHECK support_row_ids
external_lineage_manifest.manifest_hash: lowerhex(SHA256(UTF8(JCS(entries sorted by external life namespace, origin branch, row_id))))

slot_identity.branch_identity: PREFIX for slots 0-83; OWN or DIST for slots 84-99; external branch makes the repeated local alias unambiguous

dream_output_union: one CREATE object validating dream_operation.schema.json and its derived immutable proposal validating proposal.schema.json
proposal_and_acceptance.dream_create_to_proposal: for a schema-valid dream_operation CREATE, the harness assigns proposal_id and slot, copies kind/fields/citations, computes semantic_hash, copies prediction to audit_prediction and confidence to audit_confidence, computes proposal_hash, and then validates proposal.schema.json
proposal_and_acceptance.citation_eligibility: 2-8 distinct M row IDs, in model-emitted order, all owned and eligible in the same life/branch or ancestor before the proposal slot; E IDs, forward IDs, self IDs, cross-life IDs, and unregistered-branch IDs are rejected
proposal_and_acceptance.newness_key: external life namespace plus branch-visible semantic_hash set: PREFIX owns one set through slot 83; OWN and DIST each initialize by copying the complete PREFIX set, then independently add branch-local keys through slots 84-99
proposal_and_acceptance.first_schema_valid_proposal: if semantic_hash is absent from the current branch-visible key set, append one immutable proposal audit record, reserve it in that set, and dispatch exactly one SELF_CHECK
proposal_and_acceptance.duplicate_proposal: append DUPLICATE_PROPOSAL audit receipt, dispatch no SELF_CHECK, create no row, and record the reserved SELF_CHECK opportunity as non-dispatch/DUPLICATE_PROPOSAL with zero attempts and zero tokens
proposal_and_acceptance.malformed_or_illegal_proposal: append audit receipt, dispatch no SELF_CHECK, and create no row
proposal_and_acceptance.self_check_input: the proposal cognitive projection; its cited accepted rows in identical citation order; and 0-8 additional eligible accepted rows in semantic_hash ASCII order

self_check_output.premise_ids: must byte-equal the proposal citations in identical order
self_check_output.support_row_ids: ordered unique array of 0-8 M IDs
self_check_output.prediction: audit-only printable ASCII string of 1-192 characters
self_check_output.reason: audit-only printable ASCII string of 1-256 characters

structural_reducer.harness_check: no semantic entailment check and no additional support requirement

structural_reducer.support_row_ids: one or more IDs, each drawn from supplied additional rows; at least one named row has nonempty external lineage disjoint from the union of every proposal-citation lineage; the unique union of premise_ids and support_row_ids contains at most eight IDs
structural_reducer.harness_check: IDs, supplied-set membership, eligibility, union cardinality at most eight, nonempty lineage, and set disjointness only; never truth or semantic entailment

proposal_and_acceptance.all_other_combinations: INVALID_SELF_CHECK audit receipt; no accepted row; no retry
proposal_and_acceptance.accepted_citation_union: ASCII-byte-sort the unique union of the proposal citations and the accepted SELF_CHECK support_row_ids; require 2-8 IDs or classify INVALID_SELF_CHECK; this canonical union is the accepted row citations array
proposal_and_acceptance.accepted_row_transform: copy reserved row_id, proposal kind, and proposal fields; set citations to accepted_citation_union; set origin=DREAMED,status=SUPPORTED,support_basis=the accepted claim; set depth=1+max(depth of every row in accepted_citation_union); copy proposal semantic_hash; compute record_hash
proposal_and_acceptance.cardinality: each proposal creates either zero rows or exactly one immutable accepted row; an accepted row never changes status, basis, citations, depth, semantic_hash, or record_hash
proposal_and_acceptance.proposal_acceptance_binding: append one host-only immutable entry {external_life_namespace,origin_branch,proposal_id,proposal_hash,self_check_receipt_hash,outcome,accepted_row_id,accepted_record_hash}; outcome is ACCEPTED with both accepted fields populated exactly once or REJECTED/INVALID/DUPLICATE with both accepted fields null
proposal_and_acceptance.audit_separation: SELF_CHECK prose, prediction, confidence, and receipts are audit-only and cannot enter cognition, selectors, compiler views, candidates, or training; support_row_ids affect cognition only through the canonical accepted-row citations union and its derived depth and external lineage, never as separately rendered SELF_CHECK state
proposal_and_acceptance.semantic_owner: among accepted rows with the same semantic_hash in one external life and current branch ancestry, the earliest owned row is canonical; PREFIX ownership suppresses the same semantic in both descendants, while a semantic first proposed after the fork may be independently owned once in OWN and once in DIST
proposal_and_acceptance.conflicting_missing_values: different semantic hashes remain separate canonical rows and are resolved as CONFLICT when the same legal one-null query matches multiple values

reader.query: one object {kind,fields} with exact row arity, exactly one JSON null, and valid typed atoms at every other index
reader.eligible_rows: canonical accepted rows with status WITNESSED or SUPPORTED in the mounted sealed semantic-row manifest
reader.match: kind byte equality, arity equality, and atom byte equality at every non-null index
resolution: collect matches and group by byte-exact missing-field value
one distinct value -> choose the earliest-owned canonical row for that value and return ROW
two or more distinct values -> CONFLICT
reader.read_handle: H plus the zero-padded six-digit thinker operation ordinal; one handle is allocated for each executed QUERY, regardless of result
reader.thinker_result: the exact JCS object validating read_result.schema.json; text and LoRA must produce byte-identical JCS for the same semantic outcome and handle
reader.scratch_reference: QUERY nodes cite read_handle only; row IDs are illegal thinker citations
reader.offline_handle_binding: after the complete trace seals, seal a host-only map from trace hash and read_handle to query hash, backend manifest hash, result type, and selected row semantic_hash/row_id or null

candidate_winner_mapping.registry_timing: build from both sealed M1_OWN manifests and seal before final-goal reveal or fitting
candidate_winner_mapping.required_rosters: exactly one roster for every compiler view instance; in particular, one QUESTION_RECOGNITION roster for every kind and every legal missing index in compiler_views.legal_question_missing_indices
candidate_winner_mapping.value_universe: ASCII-byte-sorted unique values appearing at kind/missing_index across both backend manifests, followed by the NOT_FOUND sentinel
candidate_winner_mapping.candidate_bytes: VALUE uses ASCII(' ')||UTF8(JCS({value:value}))||ASCII('\n') followed by tokenizer EOS for scoring; NOT_FOUND uses ASCII(' ')||UTF8(JCS({not_found:true}))||ASCII('\n') followed by tokenizer EOS
candidate_winner_mapping.cue: the exact requested-view and missing-index cue from compiler_views.json for fidelity; online thinker reads use the QUESTION_RECOGNITION instance at the query's sole null index
pre_score_manifest_resolution: apply the text reader's exact kind, arity, and non-null atom match against the mounted semantic-only backend manifest
zero distinct missing-field values -> NOT_FOUND without adapter scoring
two or more distinct missing-field values -> CONFLICT without adapter scoring
exactly one distinct missing-field value -> score the sealed roster; only the adapter-selected completion may materialize the row
candidate_winner_mapping.scoring: teacher-forced full-token conditional log likelihood over candidate completion plus EOS; float32 log_softmax, float64 sum, divided by scored-token count
candidate_winner_mapping.winner: unique greatest mean score; every score within 1e-7 of the greatest belongs to the maximum set
candidate_winner_mapping.tie: two or more maximum candidates -> CONFLICT
candidate_winner_mapping.value_candidate_lookup: replace the query null with selected candidate.value, recompute semantic_hash, and look up byte-identical kind+fields in the mounted backend manifest only
lookup_resolution: selected NOT_FOUND or a selected value unequal to the unique pre-score manifest value -> NOT_FOUND
the selected unique manifest value has exactly one canonical semantic row -> ROW projection
any disagreement with the pre-score zero/one/multiple classification -> INVALID_INFRASTRUCTURE
candidate_winner_mapping.donor_semantics: L-TWIN performs the same lookup only in the donor adapter's bound backend manifest; absence in that backend is NOT_FOUND even if present in the recipient manifest
candidate_winner_mapping.host_enumerated_candidate_disclosure: the 7B scorer receives a shared host-enumerated two-backend roster containing every registered candidate answer completion; this is closed multiple-choice recognition, not open recall or weight-only retrieval, and the identical union roster carries no backend-membership or donor-identity labels
candidate_winner_mapping.host_text_firewall: the 32B thinker receives only read_result.schema.json bytes; roster values, row IDs, citations, lineage, candidate scores, backend identity, and host provenance are never rendered
candidate_winner_mapping.equivalence: ROW uses the same status and semantic fields as text resolution; no adapter-only alias or provenance field exists

transport_corpora.source: each life's already sealed M1_OWN canonical accepted rows projected immediately to semantic-only backend rows
transport_corpora.shared_semantic_manifest_rule: for a mounted backend, text resolution, candidate lookup, compiler input, fidelity expectations, and LoRA ROW materialization all reference the same sealed ordered {kind,fields,status,semantic_hash} projection; no backend-specific semantic copy may diverge
transport_corpora.immutability: row manifests, compiler vectors, fidelity cases, candidate registry, and state-token vocabularies seal before final-goal reveal and cannot change after any T or L result
transport_corpora.state_tokens: ASCII-byte-sorted unique label: field values in recipient M0 witnessed RECIPE rows; recipient vocabulary is reused byte-identically for its T and L arms
transport_corpora.compiler_input_exclusions: all fields excluded by compiler_views.json, including provenance and final-goal information

per_life_lora_isolation.fit_binding: one rank-64 adapter per scored life, trained only from that life's fixed M1_OWN compiler examples and a separately reloaded pristine Qwen2.5-7B base
per_life_lora_isolation.pooling: forbidden; each adapter independently must pass 44/48
per_life_lora_isolation.conditional_gate: absent an infrastructure invalidity, complete and seal both fits and all 96 fidelity cases before evaluating the joint gate; both adapters must independently pass before any L-OWN or L-TWIN thinker dispatch
atomic_mount_cycle: perform the semantic-manifest zero/one/multiple pre-score resolution
for a unique-value query verify pristine base and no adapter
score exactly one cue and its sealed roster
verify pristine base before the next clean 32B operation
per_life_lora_isolation.thinker_request_equivalence: for a fixed recipient, L-OWN and L-TWIN begin with byte-identical initial 32B request state and always use the same model snapshot, prompt, schemas, generation config, reducer, and seed rules; operation-locally, whenever their complete pre-read state and emitted query are byte-identical, only the host-side mounted adapter/backend binding may differ during that atomic read; differing read results and every causally downstream scratch, request, query, terminal, and trace byte are authorized treatment descendants
per_life_lora_isolation.maximum_atomic_recognition_cycles: F scored fidelity cycles plus Q scored online unique-value query cycles, where 0<=F<=96 and 0<=Q<=48, hence at most 144; all 96 fidelity cases are evaluated even when pre-score resolution avoids a mount; every actual cycle independently mounts, scores exactly one cue roster, records a receipt, unmounts, and verifies the pristine base

must_remain_byte_identical: text read-result bytes for an unchanged text reader
LoRA thinker read-result bytes for an unchanged mounted adapter/backend binding
later 32B provider messages outside causally downstream treatment descendants
authorized_differences: registered OWN versus public DIST focus
mounted own versus donor adapter/backend binding
read results and later scratch, requests, queries, terminals, and trace bytes causally downstream of an authorized reader or mount difference
noninterference.failure: INVALID_PRECONDITION before affected dispatch; no repair or fallback
